boundary: Pass 6104 JOINS two results that were already in the corpus separately. It establishes that Sp(4,3) has a canonical chirality it cannot internally reverse. It does NOT identify which of U, U* is the physical one, and it does NOT derive the Standard Model's handedness -- picking between two distinguishable options still needs an external input

half_one_already_in_corpus.content: since q = 3 is 3 mod 4, Sp(4,3) has irreducible complex characters with Frobenius-Schur indicator 0 -- non-self-dual. The Weil representation splits as W = U + U* with U not isomorphic to U*, character field Q(sqrt(-3))

half_two_from_pass_6096.content: Sp(4,3) is PERFECT with trivial abelianisation and zero index-2 normal subgroups, so it admits no nontrivial homomorphism to {+1,-1} and cannot contain a half-spin-swapping element

pass_6105_the_synthesis.the_20_and_the_4: 4 characters are quaternionic (indicator -1) and 10 are real (+1); the 20 complex ones are where the chirality lives
pass_6105_the_synthesis.the_argument: 20 of Sp(4,3)'s 34 irreducible characters are non-self-dual, so they come in genuinely distinguishable pairs U, U*. Swapping U with U* is COMPLEX CONJUGATION, which is not an inner operation -- and the group being perfect means there is no element of determinant -1 to realise it either. So the pair is distinguishable AND unswappable from inside
pass_6105_the_synthesis.what_that_means: Sp(4,3) carries a CANONICAL CHIRALITY. There are two options, they are not isomorphic, and no element of the group exchanges them
pass_6105_the_synthesis.why_nobody_saw_it: Pass 353 proved the complex structure EXISTS and treated the remaining obstruction as the det = -1 swap. Pass 6096 proved that swap cannot occur inside the group. Neither pass cited the other, and the join is the whole argument

pass_6106_scope.honest_summary: the no-go said 'the substrate cannot even pose the question'. It can. What it still cannot do is answer it by itself
pass_6106_scope.next: look for a substrate-internal quantity that distinguishes U from U* -- the Eisenstein character field Q(sqrt(-3)) has a canonical generator choice, and whether that choice is substrate-internal is the live question
pass_6106_scope.not_resolved: WHICH of U, U* is physical. Distinguishability plus unswappability gives a canonical PAIR, not a canonical MEMBER. Choosing between them still requires an input from outside the group
pass_6106_scope.resolved: the claim that chirality is unselectable from inside the substrate. It is selectable: two distinguishable options exist and the group cannot swap them
